text.p: Gibson Chemical Industries Ltd said on Wednesday that the difficult domestic and international market conditions which reduced its 1995/96 net profit by 13.7 percent would continue in the current financial year.

"The 1995/96 year has been one of positioning the company for the future. A number of changes in internal structure and strengthening of management in some areas give us cause for optimism," it said in a statement accompany the profit result.
"We believe that we have the structures in place to succeed and grow in what will continue to be difficult trading conditions," the company said.

Net profit fell to A$8.84 million in the year to June 30 from A$10.25 million. Sales fell one percent to A$161.79 million, reflecting the sale of the Vessey operation in August 1995 and the purchase of the Tak business in January 1996.
Net profit and sales rose in the United States division but fell in Australia, the United Kingdom, and New Zealand.

The company said the New Zealand business performed well despite margin pressures while cost increases led to a substantial fall in U.K. earnings. Gibson said it recently strengthened its South East Asian operations with the opening of a new Malaysia unit. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
